There is no arbitration award in the readable content of this file, so I can't quote an amount.

What I checked: all 120 extracted pages (1–141) cycle through the same six hydrological-survey blocks — basin survey text, weir/gate inspection notes, a rotated code/formula page, two filler pages, and the "weir closure approved on 8 August" page. No arbitration, no tribunal, no award, and no currency figure appears anywhere. The only numbers in the extracted text are "61 percent" (actuator fluid), "12 May" (gate 4 inspection failure), "8 August" (approvals), and "270 degrees" (page rotation) — none is an award amount, and none belongs to a legal document.

The one real gap: 21 pages were not read. Twenty of them are declared empty (no text layer and no image content, so nothing to read). **PDF page 92** is different — it has no text layer and OCR ran on it but produced nothing. That is the single page where content could exist and remain invisible to me.

So:
- Printed amount: not retrievable from the extracted text — no amount is present in any page I can read.
- PDF page number of the award: cannot be confirmed. If it is in this file, page 92 is the only candidate.

To close that gap, OCR needs to run with an explicit document language (the `RUKE_DOCUMENT_OCR_LANGUAGE` setting); it is never defaulted, which is the most likely reason page 92 came back empty. Re-upload or re-parse with that set, and I can quote the exact printed figure and its page.
